name: Mini SWE Agent
relevance: A focused coding agent for solving issues directly from the terminal.
notes: Requires Python 3.10+. Configure a model provider separately. Inventory reads the mini-swe-agent package version.

name: OpenSpec
relevance: Adds structured specifications and change planning to existing coding agents.
notes: Requires Node 20.19+. Run openspec init in each project separately to choose and configure coding-agent integrations.

name: Workmux
relevance: Provides isolated worktrees and terminal sessions for parallel coding agents.
notes: Requires git and tmux (or a supported terminal multiplexer) for agent workflows. Run workmux setup separately to install optional hooks and skills.

name: Worktrunk
relevance: Makes isolated coding-agent branches and worktree lifecycles easy to manage.
notes: This entry manages the Homebrew wt CLI on macOS/Linux. Run wt config shell install separately for directory switching. Windows installation is omitted because wt conflicts with Windows Terminal; upstream offers git-wt through Winget.

name: Gas Town
relevance: Coordinates coding agents, work assignment, durable context and merge workflows.
notes: Manages the gt CLI only. Full workflows also require configured coding agents, tmux, Dolt and Beads. Review the upstream prerequisites and initialize a workspace separately.

name: CCManager
relevance: Tracks and switches between coding-agent sessions and isolated worktrees.
notes: The npm package bundles native platform executables for macOS, Linux and Windows x64. Install and authenticate the coding agents you want to manage separately.

name: Agent Manager
relevance: Combines live coding-agent status, worktree management and review in a terminal.
notes: YoanWai Agent Manager is a separate project from AgentManager (agentmgr). Homebrew installs its tmux dependency; git and authenticated agent CLIs are needed for workflows. This entry uses the macOS/Linux formula.

name: Ralphex
relevance: Executes coding plans through repeated fresh sessions and independent reviews.
notes: Requires a supported coding executor such as Claude Code or Codex. Supply and review an implementation plan separately. The upstream Homebrew tap provides macOS/Linux binaries.

name: Oh My ClaudeCode
relevance: Adds coordinated agent teams and reusable coding workflows to Claude Code.
notes: The project is branded oh-my-claudecode; its official npm package is oh-my-claude-sisyphus. Use Node 20 or 22 through 26, as declared by the package. Configure Claude Code and run omc setup separately. Native Windows team workflows require psmux; Unix team workflows use tmux.

name: Oh My Codex
relevance: Adds agent teams, task workflows and persistent project context around Codex.
notes: Requires an installed and authenticated Codex CLI. Run scoped omx setup separately before using workflows. This entry follows the upstream recommended macOS/Linux path; native Windows is not included.

name: OmO
relevance: A standalone terminal coding agent with orchestrated multi-model workflows.
notes: Formerly oh-my-opencode; the canonical repository is oh-my-openagent. The standalone omo command is published in the official omo-ai npm package, not the unrelated omo package. Requires Node 24+. Configure providers separately.

name: ccstatusline
relevance: Shows coding-agent usage, context and repository state inside the terminal.
notes: Run the configuration TUI separately to choose status widgets and enable the Claude Code status line. Installing the package does not authorize changes to Claude Code settings.

name: Vibe Kanban
relevance: Organizes and reviews parallel coding-agent tasks in isolated workspaces.
notes: The CLI launches the local server and browser interface. Authenticate supported coding agents separately. Version probing is disabled to avoid starting the application during detection; npm inventory supplies the package version.

name: PicoClaw
relevance: A lightweight tool-using agent available through a local command-line runtime.
notes: This entry manages the Homebrew core CLI on macOS/Linux. Run onboarding and configure model providers or messaging channels separately; it does not install the launcher UI.

name: NullClaw
relevance: Provides a small local autonomous-agent runtime and configurable tool gateway.
notes: Homebrew supplies the self-contained macOS/Linux CLI. Provider configuration, onboarding and service installation are separate explicit steps.

name: Gajae Code
relevance: A standalone coding agent with repository tools and persistent terminal sessions.
notes: Uses the upstream tagged installer to fetch the latest stable standalone binary and verify published SHA-256 checksums. Bun is not required. Supports macOS x64/arm64 and glibc Linux x64/arm64; Alpine/musl is excluded. Default location is ~/.local/bin/gjc. Provider setup is separate.

name: MCPorter
relevance: Makes MCP tools discoverable and callable from coding-agent shell workflows.
notes: Requires Node 24+. The canonical repository moved from steipete/mcporter to openclaw/mcporter. Review MCP server configuration and authentication separately before connecting tools.

name: Claude Code Templates
relevance: Provides reusable coding-agent configuration and project workflow components.
notes: Installs the configuration CLI only. Run it separately to choose and review agents, hooks, settings, MCP integrations or project templates before applying them.

name: tuicr
relevance: Supports focused human review of code and diffs produced by coding agents.
notes: This entry uses the macOS/Linux Homebrew formula. Open a repository or diff explicitly to review agent-generated changes and export review feedback.

name: Spec Kit
relevance: Connects specifications, implementation plans and verification in coding-agent workflows.
notes: The official PyPI package is specify-cli and its executable is specify. Requires Python 3.11+. Run specify init separately to choose an integration and add project files. Optional extensions and presets are separate choices.
